display.purpose: **Unused.** Defined in the scale but consumed nowhere in the codebase. The largest type actually rendered is 48px (About dialog). Do not start using it without a deliberate decision.

body-base.purpose: Default reading size for dialogs, forms, and table cells.

body-sm.purpose: Panel sub-labels, meta rows, compact tags.

body-xs.purpose: Topbar chrome, timestamps, status badges, count pills.

label-md.purpose: Form labels, table headers, button text at body scale.
label-md.mapsTo: --body-md-* (note: token weight is 400 for the regular step; the 500 here refers to --body-md-strong-* / --font-weight-medium usage in labels and table headers)

metric.purpose: Counts and percentages in narrow chrome. Always tabular.

code.purpose: Codes, IDs, prices, numeric table cells. Always tabular.

shadows.name: edge
shadows.purpose: Dashboard panels. Reads as a crisp edge, not lift.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.value: 0 12px 32px color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-default) 16%, transparent), 0 2px 8px color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-default) 8%, transparent)

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.value: 0 24px 64px color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-default) 14%, transparent), 0 4px 16px color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-default) 8%, transparent)

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for sidebar and layout transitions.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover, focus, and state colour transitions — the system default.

motion.name: duration-mid
motion.purpose: Icon rotation and small positional transitions.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: Global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) override on every transition and animation.

breakpoints.name: base
breakpoints.note: Mobile; sidebar is an off-canvas drawer.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.note: Sidebar enters the grid as a 220px column.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.note: Monitor page goes to three columns.

constraints: Every colour, spacing, and radius value must be a CSS custom property reference; literal hex/px in component code is a lint error (dz/token-literal).
Template :style must not carry static styles; only per-instance computed values (dz/no-inline-style-literal).
.ds-* names must only be defined in assets/css/components.css; feature layers use their own prefix (dz/no-ds-namespace).
A theme-colour token must be added to all three blocks in theme.css (:root, .dark, and the prefers-color-scheme block) or one theme silently breaks.
Breakpoint width values are whitelisted to 640/768/1024/1280 and machine-enforced by a test.

narrative.overview: This is a system built to be glanced at, not read. Every screen answers one question — is everything still running — and the visual language is engineered for that answer to arrive in under a second, at a distance, while the operator is also watching something else. The register is deliberately generic: neutral system UI, no brand gesture, no signature flourish. This is a tool surface that should get out of the way. Density is a feature here, not a compromise. Depth is nearly absent — panels sit flat on hairlines, and elevation is reserved for things that float. Colour is spent only on state, so the chrome stays achromatic and a single amber cell is unmissable.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral system UI stack; no brand typeface, no expressive chrome
Density over breathing room; 11–15px body range, compact 32px control heights
Achromatic chrome; color reserved for state, never decoration
Flat panels, hairline separation, elevation only for overlay
Light and dark are peers, not modes — both are first-class, fully specified
Numerals get tabular figures and monospace faces; text never does

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Every chromatic family has exactly one meaning. Violet is identity, crimson/jade is direction, status hues are process state, gold is contract type. Nothing decorative is ever allowed to borrow a family.

rules.name: The Achromatic Chrome Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds, borders, text, icons, and every ordinary control are grey. If a surface needs to feel important, it gets weight or position — not hue.

rules.name: The Paired-Step Rule
rules.body: Every status color exists in three coordinated forms: a solid -default, a transparent -surface for grounds, and a text -on-surface for labels. Use them as a set.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Any figure that can change carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and usually a mono or metric face. Without this, a row of updating prices jitters.

rules.name: The No Display Type In The Shell Rule
rules.body: The 40–52px display steps exist for pre-authentication surfaces. Inside the app shell the largest type is 32px, and most of the interface lives between 11 and 17px.

rules.name: The Elevation-Is-A-Promise Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the thing is above the document and can be dismissed. Nothing that stays put gets one. Panels are not cards floating over a background; they are the background.

rules.name: The Shift-Not-Scale Rule
rules.body: Interactive feedback is a background-alpha change or a border-color change at 120ms. Nothing grows, lifts, or bounces on hover.

rules.name: The 8-And-12 Rule
rules.body: Controls are 8px, containers are 12px. A control inside a container aligns its radius to the control scale, never to the container's.

rules.name: The Hairline-Only Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px --border-neutral-l1 rule or a tonal step — never both at once, never a heavier divider to signal emphasis.

dos: Do spend colour on state and let chrome stay grey.
Do use tabular-nums and a mono face for every changing figure.
Do give every status a text label alongside its colour.
Do keep controls at 8px radius and containers at 12px.
Do pair a status -surface ground with its matching -on-surface label; the pairs are contrast-tested.
Do separate with a hairline or a tonal step — pick one.
Do specify light and dark together; both are first-class and a token added to one must be added to all three theme blocks.
Do reference tokens (var(--x)) for every colour, spacing, and radius value.
donts: Don't use brand violet for ordinary buttons, switches, or tags — it is identity, not affordance.
Don't flip rise/fall to the Western convention. Red is up.
Don't add an icon or hue to a surface that is merely important; use weight or position.
Don't enlarge type past 32px inside the app shell to signal importance.
Don't animate scale, lift, or bounce on hover — 120ms colour and background transitions only.
Don't add a shadow to something that does not float and cannot be dismissed.
Don't write literal hex, px, or radius values in component code; a lint rule fails the build.
Don't introduce a breakpoint outside the whitelisted five.
Don't use the generic disabled ink on an inverted or coloured ground — use the paired disabled token.
